flagship.headline: Peter, Paul and Mary reach No. 1 with Leaving on a Jet Plane
flagship.summary_line_1: Peter, Paul and Mary's Leaving on a Jet Plane reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 20, 1969, replacing Steam's Na Na Hey Hey Kiss Him Goodbye.
flagship.summary_line_2: The John Denver song, cut for their 1967 LP Album 1700, became the folk trio's only Hot 100 No. 1, per Wikipedia, and the clip below is the group's official lyric video.

events.headline: Peter, Paul and Mary reach No. 1 with Leaving on a Jet Plane
events.summary_line_1: Peter, Paul and Mary's Leaving on a Jet Plane reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 20, 1969, replacing Steam's Na Na Hey Hey Kiss Him Goodbye.
events.summary_line_2: The John Denver song, cut for their 1967 LP Album 1700, became the folk trio's only Hot 100 No. 1, per Wikipedia, and the clip below is the group's official lyric video.

events.headline: The Beatles send fans their sixth Christmas record
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles' 1968 Christmas Record went out free to fan-club members on December 20, 1968, as the double-sided flexi disc Lyntone LYN 1743/4, per the Lyntone catalogue at jpgr.co.uk.
events.summary_line_2: Radio 1 DJ Kenny Everett edited together pieces each Beatle recorded on his own, plus Tiny Tim singing Nowhere Man, and the clip below is the Beatles' original Nowhere Man.

events.headline: Hello, Goodbye holds No. 1 as Magical Mystery Tour leaps to No. 3
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles' Hello, Goodbye was No. 1 on the UK chart dated December 20, 1967, while their Magical Mystery Tour double EP jumped from No. 20 to No. 3, per the Official Charts Company.
events.summary_line_2: The Monkees' Daydream Believer climbed from No. 13 to No. 8 the same week, and the clip below is the Beatles' official Hello, Goodbye film.

events.headline: The Beatles add backing vocals to When I'm Sixty-Four
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles worked on When I'm Sixty-Four at EMI Studios in London on December 20, 1966, with John Lennon, Paul McCartney and George Harrison adding backing vocals, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Arriving that evening, each Beatle gave a short interview for ITV's Reporting '66, aired on December 29, per the same archive, and the clip below is the finished song from Sgt. Pepper.

events.headline: Wilson Pickett records 634-5789 at Stax
events.summary_line_1: Wilson Pickett recorded 634-5789 (Soulsville, U.S.A.) at Stax Studios in Memphis on December 20, 1965, with Steve Cropper, Duck Dunn, Al Jackson Jr. and Isaac Hayes behind him, per MusicBrainz.
events.summary_line_2: The Eddie Floyd and Steve Cropper song became a No. 1 R&B hit for the soul shouter in 1966, per Wikipedia, and the clip below is the original recording.

events.headline: Memphis jug band star Charlie Burse dies at 64
events.summary_line_1: Charlie Burse, the singer and guitarist known as "Uke" from the Memphis Jug Band, died of heart disease in Memphis on December 20, 1965, per his Wikipedia biography, citing Eagle and LeBlanc's Blues: A Regional Experience.
events.summary_line_2: His jug band records with Will Shade were part of the blues revival that fed 1960s folk and rock, and the clip below is Oil It Up and Go by Charlie Burse and His Memphis Mudcats.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones play the Lido Ballroom in Winchester
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones played the Lido Ballroom in Winchester, England, on December 20, 1963, per the Time Is On Our Side gig archive and the Rolling Stones Data chronology.
events.summary_line_2: Their Lennon and McCartney single I Wanna Be Your Man stood at No. 13 on the UK chart dated December 19, per the Official Charts Company, and the clip below is that single.

events.headline: The Osmond Brothers make their TV debut with Andy Williams
events.summary_line_1: The Osmond Brothers, Alan, Wayne, Merrill and Jay, first appeared on NBC's The Andy Williams Show on December 20, 1962, per Wikipedia's history of the show, citing the Complete Directory to Prime Time Network TV Shows.
events.summary_line_2: They became the show's regular backing singers for the rest of its run, and the clip below, from Donny Osmond's official channel, shows the brothers on Andy Williams's 1966 Christmas special.

events.headline: The Beatles play night three of their last Star-Club run
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Star-Club in Hamburg on December 20, 1962, the third night of their final residency there, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Back home Love Me Do sat at No. 22 on the UK chart dated that same day, per the Official Charts Company, and the clip below is the debut single itself.

events.headline: Return to Sender holds No. 1 for Elvis Presley in Britain
events.summary_line_1: Elvis Presley's Return to Sender was No. 1 on the UK chart dated December 20, 1962, per the Official Charts listing.
events.summary_line_2: Cliff Richard's The Next Time and Bachelor Boy jumped from No. 5 to No. 2 behind it the same week, and the clip below is Elvis's official audio.

events.headline: The Beatles play an evening show at the Cavern Club
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played an evening session at the Cavern Club in Liverpool on December 20, 1961, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Their first record, My Bonnie, cut with Tony Sheridan in Hamburg that June, had come out in Germany in October, per Wikipedia, and the clip below is that recording.
